US-119-S283.title: Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act
US-119-S283.summary:
Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act

This act directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to jointly develop a standard methodology for identifying the country of origin of seafood to support enforcement against illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing (IUU fishing) and seafood fraud.

NOAA and NIST must consult with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the Coast Guard in developing the methodology, which must use chemical analysis to identify the country of origin of seafood. The methodology must be consistent with the needs of federal and state law enforcement agencies in combating IUU fishing and seafood fraud. The methodology must also include a portable field kit and, to the extent practicable, be appropriate for testing prepared food (including raw preparations of seafood such as sushi). The agencies must conduct pilot studies of the methodology on red snapper and tuna.

Within two years after the act's enactment, NIST must report to Congress regarding the methodology and a plan for operationalizing it. The report must explain any aspects of its methodology that are impracticable, whether additional research would make the methodology practicable, and whether an alternate approach might be practicable.

US-119-S283.aiSummary: This law tells NOAA and NIST to work together on a standard way to find where seafood comes from, to help stop illegal fishing and seafood fraud. They must use chemical testing, work with Customs and Border Protection and the Coast Guard, and make a portable field kit that can also be used on some prepared seafood like sushi when possible. They must test the method on red snapper and tuna, and NIST must report to Congress within two years on the method and how it could be used in practice.

US-119-HR9191.title: National Fossil Act of 2026
US-119-HR9191.summary:
National Fossil Act of 2026

This bill designates the Mammut americanum (the American Mastodon) fossil as the national fossil mammal and the Tyrannosaurus rex fossil as the national fossil dinosaur.

US-119-HR10180.title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10180.description: To amend the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to authorize certain assessments by the Director of the Institute and impose requirements on certain memorandums of understanding relating to artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10180.aiSummary: The bill would let the National Institute of Standards and Technology director assess trends in artificial intelligence system abilities, including whether AI can help make new AI systems. It would also set rules for agreements with developers of frontier AI systems, which are leading-edge systems, before pre-deployment testing. Those agreements would have to allow the director to ask for details about how AI was used to help build the system and include testing for that ability.

US-119-S4908.title: Gas Money Saved Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4908.description: A bill to require the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to initiate a process to reevaluate corporate average fuel economy standards, and for other purposes.
US-119-S4908.aiSummary: The bill would tell the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to review fuel economy rules if gas prices rise much faster than overall inflation over a 180-day period. It would also raise the fuel economy penalty amounts in federal law from $0 to $25 and $50. This would affect the agency and car makers that must meet those standards.

US-119-HJRES35.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems: Procedures for Facilitating Compliance, Including Netting and Exemptions".
US-119-HJRES35.summary:
This joint resolution eliminates an annual waste emissions charge on oil or gas facilities under the Methane Emissions Reduction Program. Under the program, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) currently collects a waste emissions charge from specific types of oil or gas facilities, such as onshore or offshore facilities that produce oil or gas, for exceeding emission thresholds for greenhouse gas emissions and methane emissions.

Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies the rule titled Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems: Procedures for Facilitating Compliance, Including Netting and Exemptions and published by the EPA on November 18, 2024.
